title: Sharp Variance Corrections for Pooled Follow-Up Sampling after Attrition under a Hard Budget
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but achieved subfield below field floor; cold paper score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4 and not salvageable in scope, independently validity-gate confirmed.
gap_reasons: The delivered characterization establishes positive, optimized n^-2 interior and n^-3/2 saturation corrections for binary outcomes, balanced assignment, and perfect pooled recovery; it does not establish refined observed-record coverage or sharpness beyond this design.

Observed-record inference relies on exhaustive margin and completion enumeration followed by Chebyshev calibration, without an implemented demonstration of computational feasibility or useful interval lengths.

The enormous interior remainder constant, crossover certificate without an explicit convergence rate, and small validation examples leave the corrections’ practical importance after margin uncertainty unresolved.
paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed the uniform second-order interior variance envelope, strict positivity, integer transportation optimizers, and an additional saturation crossover with an n^-3/2 stop-loss term. The final mathematics panel passed with no findings, but the cold tier review and independent validity audit capped the result at subfield below the standing field floor; two bounded positioning findings remain. No Lean formalization was launched, and a future re-raise needs a materially stronger inferential or design theorem rather than an identical retry.
tldr: Initial attrition changes which enrolled subjects contribute to an experimental contrast. Uniform guaranteed recovery from one common hard-budget pool restores unbiasedness, but its random pool denominator leaves uncertainty about the joint potential responses. The result gives two sharp first corrections to the worst-case variance envelope over every compatible hidden integer completion: a strictly positive \(n^{-2}\) coefficient \(K\) on each fixed strictly undersaturated interior \(\mathcal I_\epsilon\), and a strictly positive \(n^{-3/2}\) Gaussian stop-loss coefficient on compact actual saturation offsets \(\mathcal J_{\epsilon,S_{\mathrm c}}\). Exact forest procedures give full-completion upper certificates and integer tables attaining the evaluated coefficients. Original-record hypergeometric inversion supplies finite conservative inference. Intensive tracking in Molina-Millán and Macours motivates a prospective guaranteed-recovery protocol; their historical procedure is not asserted to implement this design.
gap: Complete-record covariance bounds do not evaluate the pooled reciprocal audit expectation after maximizing over hidden joint responses. Regular double sampling supplies the phase decomposition, while the supplied preliminary derivation leaves total-coefficient noncancellation unresolved.
fill: The deliverable evaluates every correction branch with actual integer margins and budgets, certifies an upper bound over the entire completion class, and resolves the first surviving correction through \(\texttt{oeq:first-nonzero-frontier}\). A total finite margin region handles the uncertainty in using the envelope for enrolled-cohort ITT calibration.
